disease_mechanism_summary: SPG8 is an autosomal dominant hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by heterozygous, mostly missense variants in WASHC5/strumpellin, a core subunit of the pentameric WASH complex that drives actin-dependent sorting and recycling at endosomes (EVIDENCE, supportive, MONDO:0011339). The inferred cellular consequence is impaired endosomal actin nucleation with downstream endolysosomal dysfunction; the only direct experimental support that a patient-equivalent variant (N471D) causes endolysosomal defects and loses normal interaction partners comes from Dictyostelium (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:30061306) — a non-neuronal, non-heterozygous system. Two decision-critical uncertainties remain unresolved. First, the allelic mechanism: a mouse knockout report suggesting heterozygous animals lack a motor phenotype argues against simple haploinsufficiency and favours a toxic/interfering allele, but this detail was recalled rather than confirmed in full text (INFERENCE, contradictory/inconclusive, PMID:26572744), while earlier cell work proposed haploinsufficiency. This inverts the sign of any genetic intervention: lower the mutant transcript, or raise wild-type strumpellin. Second, the causal step from endosomal mis-sorting to length-dependent corticospinal axon degeneration is entirely unestablished; length-dependent pathology is imported from HSP as a class, not demonstrated for WASHC5 (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, MONDO:0011339). No human SPG8 cellular phenotype — endolysosomal, transport, or axonal — was retrieved in this work (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied). No validated in vivo SPG8 model reproducing spastic paraplegia was identified, and no patient-missense knock-in mouse (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID:26572744). Net: the gene is solid, the cell biology is plausible but unmeasured in human SPG8 neurons, and the therapeutic direction is undetermined.
leverage_points: Allelic sign determination in an isogenic human neuron trio (patient missense heterozygote / variant-corrected / WASHC5 heterozygous null). This single construct answers dominant-negative vs haploinsufficiency and simultaneously creates the phenotype assay every other approach needs. It is the highest-information, lowest-cost node in the whole program (INFERENCE, supportive).

WASH complex integrity as a direct, mechanism-proximal readout: co-immunoprecipitation of WASHC1/2/3/4 with mutant vs wild-type strumpellin. Loss of interactors is the one effect actually demonstrated for a patient-equivalent variant (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:30061306), making it the most defensible first assay rather than a bulk lysosomal marker.

Separating the recycling arm from the degradative arm of the endolysosomal readout. WASH-dependent failure traps cargo that should be recycled; a flux-enhancing drug would then accelerate loss of exactly that cargo while improving a lysosomal biomarker. Measuring both arms separately converts a likely false-positive into a detectable directional-harm signal (INFERENCE, supportive).

WASHC5 haplotype structure across SPG8 families — a cheap long-read phasing question that determines whether anything beyond an n-of-1 oligonucleotide product can ever exist (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:33209959; PMID:31708117).

Small molecules are the only modality whose delivery reaches the putative site of failure. The distal corticospinal axon is intracellular cytoplasm tens of centimetres from a deep layer-V soma; small molecules diffuse there once past the BBB, oligonucleotides must act in a poorly exposed soma, and proteins reach neither (INFERENCE, supportive).

Existing, well-characterised selective CNS-penetrant HDAC6 inhibitors provide a ready pharmacological probe if — and only if — a baseline transport/acetylation deficit is first demonstrated (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:41061670; PMID:29520015; PMID:31845794).

reviews.why_it_could_work: A dominant missense variant in a core subunit of an obligate multiprotein complex is the classic genetic architecture for a poisoning allele, and the one patient-equivalent variant studied is expressed and mis-functions with loss of interactors rather than being absent — the precondition for mutant lowering to help (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:30061306; MONDO:0011339). Absence of a motor phenotype in heterozygous knockout mice, if confirmed, further argues the problem is not missing protein (INFERENCE, supportive, PMID:26572744). Single-nucleotide allele discrimination by RNase-H gapmers is a solved design problem in principle, with >100-fold selectivity demonstrated and stereopure SNP-selective chemistry validated in vivo (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:23963702; PMID:39027419), and intrathecal ASO dosing is an approved, repeatable CNS route (INFERENCE, supportive). Crucially the same reagent set is the cleanest instrument to resolve the mechanism, so the money buys an answer even if it never buys a drug.
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Two, compounding. (1) Sign error: if WASHC5 is dosage-limiting, lowering is neutral at best and any wild-type off-allele knockdown is actively harmful — the direction of the required transcript change is not established in any human neuronal system (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID:26572744). (2) Target-cell coverage: excellent in-vitro allele selectivity did not translate into clinical benefit for SNP-phased mutant HTT ASOs, which were discontinued (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:33209959), and the SPG8 cell that must be silenced — the deep layer-V corticospinal soma — is among the least well-exposed compartments after intrathecal dosing (INFERENCE, contradictory). Neither failure mode has been tested. Beyond these, private scattered variants mean an n-of-1 product unless haplotype clustering exists, which is unstudied (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied), and no HSP oligonucleotide program exists to borrow a path from (EVIDENCE, contradictory, ClinicalTrials.gov search returning 0 studies).
reviews.rationale: The proposed three-arm isogenic neuron experiment is the best-designed study in this dossier and the one piece of work I would fund first. It attacks the dominant failure mode (sign error) directly rather than deferring it, includes the heterozygous-null line as an explicit haploinsufficiency mimic, gates on allele-resolved mRNA pharmacology before interpreting biology, and pre-commits to a kill decision. The parallel long-read phasing arm is cheap and answers whether any population-scale product is possible. I do not grant PURSUE: the therapeutic hypothesis itself rests on an unconfirmed recalled mouse result plus a Dictyostelium variant, there is no human neuronal evidence of dominant-negative action, and the second failure mode — knockdown in deep cortical somata — is untested and has already sunk the closest clinical precedent. The honest framing in the upstream work, that the first use of these tools is mechanistic rather than therapeutic, is correct and should be held to: fund the probe, not the program. One caution on the experiment as written — if no phenotype separates patient from corrected neurons, that is the most likely outcome given nothing has ever been measured in human SPG8 cells, and the design rightly calls this an assay failure rather than a negative.

reviews.why_it_could_work: Identical biological rationale to the ASO arm (EVIDENCE, supportive, MONDO:0011339; PMID:30061306). RNAi acts in the cytoplasm on mature mRNA, which suits a missense, non-splicing target, and seed-positioned single-nucleotide discrimination is established in principle for other dominant alleles (INFERENCE, supportive). The proposed wild-type-loss tolerance curve is genuinely valuable independent of modality because it quantifies WASHC5 dosage sensitivity in human neurons — the same number that decides whether a wild-type-raising program is the right answer instead.
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Biodistribution, aggravated by dosage risk. Intrathecal siRNA plausibly silences superficial cortex, cord and glia far better than deep layer-V somata, producing the worst possible distribution: near-complete knockdown in bystander cells where wild-type loss is pure liability, and partial knockdown in the one neuron that matters (INFERENCE, contradictory). No siRNA is approved for any CNS indication, and no RNA program exists in any HSP — the only genetic HSP trials retrieved are AAV gene addition in recessive AP4-HSP, out of scope (EVIDENCE, contradictory, NCT06948019; NCT05518188). This liability cannot be de-risked in any currently available system, since no in vivo SPG8 model exists.
reviews.rationale: The proposed reporter-first selectivity triage against an independently measured tolerance curve is a disciplined, cheap design, and the upstream agent is admirably explicit that RNAi is the second-choice reagent behind the ASO. I agree with that sequencing and formalise it: this duplicates the ASO arm's mechanistic question while carrying a strictly worse CNS delivery position — intrathecal ASOs have approved human precedent in motor neuron disease, CNS siRNA has none. Funding both in parallel buys one answer twice. The genuinely non-duplicative element is the wild-type-loss tolerance curve, which should be run once, in the ASO workstream, as a dose-titration of a total-WASHC5 knockdown reagent in control neurons. Reopen this modality only if the ASO format fails on chemistry (not on biology) or if durability data make a di-siRNA architecture decisively superior.

reviews.why_it_could_work: It is the hypothesis most robust to the central allelic uncertainty: acting downstream of WASHC5, it would serve all genotypes with a far simpler development path, and brain-penetrant mTORC1 inhibitors are already clinically available with demonstrated human CNS target engagement, so a validated node would need no new chemistry (INFERENCE, supportive). An endolysosomal defect is the one phenotype actually observed for a patient-equivalent strumpellin variant (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:30061306).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Directional harm masked by a successful-looking biomarker. WASH-dependent sorting failure plausibly traps cargo that should be recycled; increasing degradative flux would then accelerate loss of that cargo while normalising the lysosomal readout — the intervention is wrong-signed, not merely ineffective (INFERENCE, contradictory). Compounding this: no SPG8 pharmacological rescue of any endolysosomal phenotype was retrieved (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, PubMed query 'WASH complex strumpellin endosomal sorting rescue' — 0 results), no TFEB/lysosomal-biogenesis pharmacology has been linked to any HSP (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PubMed query 'TFEB activator trehalose neuron lysosomal biogenesis hereditary spastic paraplegia' — 0 results), so the node is transplanted pathway logic; mTORC1 inhibition suppresses local axonal translation needed for axon maintenance, i.e. the probe can injure the target compartment; and chronic systemic immunosuppression from childhood in a lifelong disease is a serious tolerability liability. Most basically, no human SPG8 cell has been shown to have any endolysosomal flux deficit at all (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied) — there is no pharmacodynamic endpoint and no dose-selection basis.
reviews.rationale: The two-stage phenotype-before-pharmacology design is correct and its best feature is the mandatory directionality controls — reading recycling cargo and axon integrity on the same plates as the lysosomal marker, so that 'biomarker improved, cargo and axons worse' is detectable rather than scored as success. That is the single most valuable thing this design can produce. But Stage 1 is a generic question — does any human SPG8 cell have a measurable trafficking phenotype — and it is answered more informatively inside the allele-dosage experiment, which asks the same question with isogenic controls and simultaneously fixes the therapeutic sign. Fibroblast-first screening on heterozygous missense effects also risks an underpowered false negative with donor variance. LOW PRIORITY rather than REJECT because the biology is the closest thing SPG8 has to a demonstrated phenotype and the repurposing path is genuinely short if a degradative-capacity deficit is found. Do not fund the compound arm. Fold Stage 1's recycling-arm and degradative-arm readouts into the isogenic neuron panel as separate, never-collapsed measures; revisit only if that panel shows a degradative-capacity deficit rather than an isolated recycling failure.

reviews.hypothesis_name: Distal axon maintenance in long corticospinal tracts
reviews.why_it_could_work: The underlying pathway hypothesis — length-dependent corticospinal degeneration intersecting with defective actin-based cargo handling — is coherent (EVIDENCE, supportive, MONDO:0011339; PMID:30061306), and receptor-mediated transcytosis shuttles are a genuine advancing route for getting proteins into CNS parenchyma, so a surface-receptor-agonist biologic is not categorically impossible (INFERENCE, inconclusive).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Target-compartment mismatch, which is categorical rather than quantitative. The requested perturbation — restore intra-axonal transport and cytoskeletal stability — has no extracellular interface for a biologic to engage, and strumpellin itself is an obligate cytosolic multiprotein-complex subunit, so protein replacement is mechanistically excluded regardless of allelic mechanism (INFERENCE, contradictory). The compartment that must be reached, the distal axon of a deep layer-V neuron, is the least accessible in the body for a systemically dosed protein; BBB shuttles deliver cargo to the endolysosome, not the cytosol. Systemic and intrathecal neurotrophic biologics (BDNF, CNTF, GDNF, IGF-1) have a long record of failure in motor neuron disease on precisely these exposure grounds (INFERENCE, contradictory), and no in vivo SPG8 model exists in which engagement could be shown (EVIDENCE, contradictory, MONDO:0011339). The predictable outcome is a well-characterised biologic that demonstrably never reaches its compartment, with a non-specific trophic readout that cannot distinguish SPG8 benefit from generic neuroprotection.
reviews.rationale: I endorse the upstream agent's own conclusion of NO PLAUSIBLE DELIVERY PATH and its refusal to propose a therapeutic experiment. The modality is excluded by compartment, not by potency or PK, and no amount of protein engineering fixes a target with no extracellular epitope. The proposed surface-proteomics and conditioned-medium screen is a legitimate prerequisite question — does any surface or secreted mediator sit between WASH-complex failure and axonal dieback — and it is cheap. But it is target discovery, not a protein program, and its most likely result is negative. If it is run at all it should be run as an add-on to the isogenic iPSC neuron work already funded for other reasons, not as a protein-modality line item. REJECT applies to the modality; the surface-biology question can live elsewhere at near-zero marginal cost.

reviews.hypothesis_name: Distal axon maintenance in long corticospinal tracts
reviews.why_it_could_work: This is the only approach whose delivery profile matches the presumed site of failure: small molecules diffuse into distal axonal cytoplasm once past the BBB, HDAC6 is cytosolic and ubiquitous so there is no cell-type uptake problem, and next-generation inhibitors were explicitly engineered for CNS penetrance (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:41061670). It is genotype-agnostic and sidesteps the unresolved allelic question entirely. The closest precedents are strong: potent HDAC6 inhibitors rescue mitochondrial axonal transport in primary neurons modelling a dominantly acting inherited axonopathy, CMT2F/HSPB1 (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:31845794), and in CMT2D mice HDAC6 inhibition restored tubulin acetylation, rescued transport and improved motor function in vivo — showing this pharmacology can convert a transport deficit into motor benefit in a length-dependent axonopathy (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:29520015). Downstream pathway modulation reaching phase III in inherited axonopathy is precedented (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:37455204). Assays and tool compounds are off the shelf, making this the most executable approach.
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: False-positive rescue. HDAC6 inhibition boosts transport in almost any cultured neuron, so SPG8 cultures will very likely 'improve' whether or not transport failure drives the disease; the program then advances on a real but disease-irrelevant pharmacodynamic effect into an ultra-rare, rapidly progressing population with no animal model and no biomarker, and discovers the error at the clinical endpoint (INFERENCE, contradictory). Underneath sits an unshown mechanistic bridge: WASH-dependent sorting is actin-based while HDAC6 inhibition acts chiefly on microtubule acetylation, so the pharmacology may address a different cytoskeletal system than the one SPG8 disrupts (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID:30061306). All transport-rescue evidence comes from CMT2D/CMT2F and amyloid models, none from WASHC5 or any HSP (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:31845794; PMID:29520015). No transport deficit has been demonstrated in SPG8 neurons (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied), no in vivo SPG8 system exists (EVIDENCE, contradictory, MONDO:0011339), chronic childhood-onset dosing of a non-cell-selective inhibitor is an untested safety question, and early onset with rapid progression may require presymptomatic initiation.
reviews.rationale: This is the best-engineered experiment against the dominant failure mode in the dossier. Two features earn the verdict: Stage 1 measures the baseline deficit before any drug is bought, so the hypothesis can die cheaply; and Stage 2 requires genotype-selective rescue, pre-specifying that an equal effect in isogenic controls at the same acetylation increase is a null result, not a hit. That directly neutralises the false-positive mode that would otherwise carry this program to an expensive clinical failure. Pre-registration of effect sizes before unblinding genotype, multiple patient lines with distinct variants, and the insistence that cellular rescue alone is insufficient to enter patients without first building a knock-in mouse are all correct. Not PURSUE: the causal chain from WASH failure to microtubule-based transport failure is assumed rather than shown, the supporting rescue data come entirely from other genes, and an untested dominant failure mode plus a missing in vivo model must not be outranked by a good-sounding mechanism and convenient tool compounds. Fund Stage 1 only, alongside the allele-dosage experiment — they share the same iPSC lines and differentiations, so the marginal cost is modest.

comparative_judgment:
The two approaches worth money are the allele-selective ASO and the HDAC6 transport probe, and they are worth money for opposite reasons. The ASO arm addresses the actual disease mechanism and is the only route that could be disease-modifying at the root, but its therapeutic sign is undetermined and its delivery to deep layer-V corticospinal somata is unproven. The HDAC6 arm addresses only a presumed final common pathway with no WASHC5-specific evidence, but it is the sole approach whose delivery reaches the compartment where SPG8 is believed to fail. Neither earns PURSUE, because in both cases the dominant failure mode is untested, and I will not let the ASO's superior mechanistic logic outrank its missing delivery evidence nor let HDAC6's ready tool compounds outrank a mechanistic bridge that has never been demonstrated.

Within the lowering hypothesis, oligonucleotide clearly beats RNA. The biology, the mechanistic question and the isogenic-neuron experiment are identical, so the comparison turns entirely on delivery and precedent: intrathecal RNase-H gapmers have approved human CNS use in motor neuron disease, whereas no siRNA is approved for any CNS indication, and intrathecal siRNA's likely distribution — strong silencing of superficial cortex, cord and glia, weak silencing of deep layer-V somata — is the worst possible pattern when wild-type loss in bystander cells may itself be harmful. Running both buys one answer twice. The single non-duplicative element of the RNA plan, the wild-type-loss tolerance curve, should be executed once inside the ASO workstream as a total-knockdown dose titration in control neurons; it quantifies WASHC5 dosage sensitivity and is informative whichever way the mechanism falls.

Within the distal-axon hypothesis, small molecule beats protein decisively and not by degree. The requested perturbation is intracellular and cytoskeletal, with no extracellular epitope, and strumpellin is an obligate cytosolic complex subunit, so protein replacement is mechanistically excluded. Small molecules diffuse to the distal axon; biologics reach neither the compartment nor the cell. This is a categorical exclusion, which is why one modality is INVESTIGATE and the other REJECT under the same biological hypothesis.

The endolysosomal flux approach sits between: its biology is the closest thing SPG8 has to a demonstrated phenotype, but its Stage 1 question — does any human SPG8 cell show a trafficking deficit — is answered better and at lower marginal cost inside the allele-dosage experiment, which asks the same thing with isogenic controls and simultaneously fixes the therapeutic sign. Its compound arm risks a wrong-signed intervention that improves a lysosomal biomarker while accelerating loss of the very cargo WASH-dependent recycling should retrieve. Its most valuable contribution is methodological and should be absorbed rather than separately funded: always read the recycling arm and the degradative arm separately, never collapsed into one score, and always alongside an axon-integrity measure.

The practical consequence is one shared experimental platform, not four programs. A single isogenic iPSC trio — patient missense heterozygote, variant-corrected, WASHC5 heterozygous null — differentiated once to cortical projection neurons, serves the allele-dosage question, the recycling-versus-degradative phenotype panel, and the baseline transport/acetylation measurement. Nearly all remaining uncertainty collapses onto that one construct.

What would change my mind. Toward PURSUE for the ASO: confirmation in full text that heterozygous Washc5 knockout mice lack a motor phenotype, plus a replicating WASH-complex or cargo phenotype in patient neurons that mutant-selective knockdown reverses while the heterozygous-null line stays normal, plus evidence that WASHC5 mutant alleles cluster on a small number of haplotypes. Toward PURSUE for HDAC6: a reproducible baseline transport or acetylation deficit across independent patient lines with genotype-selective rescue. Toward REJECT for the ASO: a heterozygous-null line that phenocopies the patient, which would invert the program to raising wild-type strumpellin. Toward REJECT for HDAC6: equal drug effect in patient and isogenic control neurons at matched acetylation. Reopening the protein modality requires one specific finding — a reproducibly altered surface receptor or secreted mediator in SPG8 neurons — and nothing less. A credible in vivo system, a patient-missense knock-in mouse showing a motor phenotype, would materially raise every approach here, since its absence is currently the shared ceiling on all of them.
what_is_known: The causal gene is solid: SPG8 is HSP caused by heterozygous, mostly missense variants in WASHC5, encoding strumpellin, a core subunit of the pentameric WASH complex (EVIDENCE, supportive, MONDO:0011339). Genotype-phenotype is otherwise thin and variants are private and scattered across the gene.

The only direct functional data on a patient-equivalent variant: strumpellin N471D in Dictyostelium causes endolysosomal system defects and loses several normal interaction partners — i.e. the mutant protein is made and mis-functions rather than being absent (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:30061306). This is the precondition for any mutant-lowering strategy, but it comes from a non-neuronal, non-heterozygous organism.

A mouse knockout study re-examining haploinsufficiency reportedly found no motor phenotype in heterozygous animals, arguing against loss of one copy being sufficient (INFERENCE, contradictory to haploinsufficiency, PMID:26572744). This detail was recalled rather than confirmed in full text and is load-bearing for the entire lowering program — it must be verified before it is relied upon.

No validated in vivo SPG8 model reproducing spastic paraplegia was identified, and no patient-missense knock-in mouse exists (EVIDENCE, contradictory, MONDO:0011339; INFERENCE, PMID:26572744). This is the shared ceiling on every approach: no cellular rescue can currently be converted into a motor-benefit demonstration.

No human SPG8 cellular phenotype — endolysosomal, cargo-sorting, transport or axonal — has been demonstrated in anything retrieved (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied). There is therefore no pharmacodynamic endpoint and no biomarker for any program.

Negative search results that matter: no SPG8 pharmacological rescue of any endolysosomal phenotype (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, PubMed 'WASH complex strumpellin endosomal sorting rescue' — 0 results); no TFEB/lysosomal-biogenesis pharmacology linked to any HSP (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PubMed 'TFEB activator trehalose neuron lysosomal biogenesis hereditary spastic paraplegia' — 0 results); no HSP antisense oligonucleotide trial (EVIDENCE, contradictory, ClinicalTrials.gov — 0 studies). Absence of literature is not evidence against these hypotheses in an ultra-rare disease, but it does mean no borrowed path exists.

A relevant prior clinical failure: SNP-phased allele-selective ASOs against mutant HTT (WVE-120101/120102) achieved excellent in-vitro selectivity yet were discontinued for lack of demonstrable benefit (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:33209959). In-vitro allele discrimination does not guarantee sufficient mutant lowering in the relevant deep CNS neurons.

Enabling precedents for allele-selective design do exist: positional-chemistry RNase-H ASOs with >100-fold single-nucleotide discrimination (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:23963702); stereopure PS/PN SNP-targeting ASOs with durable allele-selective lowering in vivo (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:39027419); validated long-read haplotype phasing workflows without family data (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:33209959) and the HD haplotype-coverage template (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:31708117).

Intrathecal ASO dosing is an approved, repeatable CNS route in motor neuron disease (nusinersen, tofersen), so route and chronic-dosing risk are not the novel part of a lowering program (INFERENCE, supportive). No siRNA is approved for any CNS indication.

Ready-made axonal-transport pharmacology exists: EKZ-438, a highly selective (>8500-fold) CNS-penetrant HDAC6 inhibitor at 12 nM characterised in neurodegeneration models (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:41061670); HDAC6 inhibitors rescue mitochondrial axonal transport in CMT2F primary neurons (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:31845794); and in CMT2D mice HDAC6 inhibition restored tubulin acetylation, rescued transport and improved motor function in vivo (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:29520015). None of this evidence involves WASHC5 or any HSP.

Failed precedent for the protein modality: systemic and intrathecal neurotrophic biologics (BDNF, CNTF, GDNF, IGF-1/mecasermin) have a long record of failure in motor neuron disease, substantially on CNS exposure grounds (INFERENCE, contradictory).

Existing HSP genetic programs on ClinicalTrials.gov are AAV gene addition in recessive AP4-related SPG47/SPG50 (EVIDENCE, NCT06948019; NCT05518188) — out of scope here and not transferable to a dominant missense disease.
critical_gaps: The therapeutic sign is unknown: dominant-negative (lower mutant) versus haploinsufficiency (raise wild-type). This inverts every genetic intervention and currently blocks all downstream spend (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID:26572744).

No measurable human SPG8 cellular phenotype exists. Without a quantitative, replicating neuronal readout there is no pharmacodynamic endpoint, no dose selection, and no way to distinguish therapeutic benefit from directional harm for any modality (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).

The load-bearing heterozygous-knockout mouse result is recalled, not verified in full text. One cheap full-text check materially changes confidence in the whole lowering rationale (INFERENCE, PMID:26572744).

No in vivo SPG8 system. Without a patient-missense knock-in mouse showing a motor phenotype, no approach can demonstrate that a cellular rescue translates into motor benefit (EVIDENCE, contradictory, MONDO:0011339).

Unknown whether the lesion is a recycling/retrieval failure or a degradative-capacity deficit. These demand opposite interventions, and a flux-enhancing drug would worsen the former while improving its biomarker (INFERENCE, contradictory).

Whether an SPG8 iPSC line with a characterised missense variant actually exists and is obtainable, and whether SPG8 families are reachable for phasing and sample donation. Availability was assumed, not verified, in the upstream work.

Whether WASHC5 mutant alleles cluster on a few common haplotypes. If not, nothing beyond an n-of-1 oligonucleotide product is possible, which changes the economics and the regulatory path entirely (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).

Whether quantitative allele-specific knockdown is achievable in deep layer-V corticospinal somata after intrathecal dosing. This is unproven for any program and sank the closest clinical precedent (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:33209959).
Whether any transport or tubulin-acetylation abnormality exists in SPG8 neurons at all; the actin-to-microtubule mechanistic bridge is assumed (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID:30061306).

next_actions.action: Verify the full text of the Washc5 knockout mouse report and audit availability of SPG8 patient material: confirm whether heterozygous animals truly lack a motor phenotype and what was measured; in parallel, canvass HSP registries, biobanks and patient foundations for existing SPG8 iPSC lines or fibroblasts with characterised missense variants, and for families willing to donate samples. Budget: weeks, minimal cost, no wet work.
next_actions.question_answered: Is the central argument against haploinsufficiency real, and do the cells and families needed for every downstream experiment actually exist?
next_actions.activity_required: Full-text retrieval and critical appraisal of PMID:26572744; outreach to HSP registries, biobanks and patient organisations; inventory of available SPG8 genotypes and consented donors.
next_actions.supports_if: The knockout paper confirms absent motor phenotype in heterozygotes on adequate testing, and at least one SPG8 patient line (ideally two distinct missense variants) is obtainable or derivable from a consented donor. Proceed immediately to the isogenic trio.
next_actions.kills_if: The mouse report does not support the recalled claim, or heterozygotes show a motor phenotype — the dominant-negative rationale weakens sharply and the program should reorient toward wild-type raising. Separately, if no patient material is reachable, the entire dossier is blocked on sample access and that, not biology, becomes the thing to fund.

next_actions.action: Build the shared platform: one isogenic human iPSC trio — SPG8 missense heterozygote, CRISPR variant-corrected, and WASHC5 heterozygous null — differentiated to cortical projection neurons, with patient fibroblasts as a cheap pre-screen. This single construct serves the allele-dosage question, the trafficking phenotype panel and the transport measurement.
next_actions.question_answered: Does any reproducible, quantifiable cellular phenotype distinguish SPG8 neurons from isogenic controls, and does a heterozygous null phenocopy the patient?
next_actions.activity_required: Line derivation/editing and QC; cortical projection neuron differentiation across >=3 independent batches; blinded, randomised, pre-registered phenotype panel reading WASH complex co-IP integrity (WASHC1/2/3/4 with strumpellin), endosomal F-actin patch density, recycling-arm cargo measures (surface:total and recycling kinetics of transferrin receptor, GLUT1, CI-MPR) and degradative-arm measures (DQ-BSA proteolysis, cathepsin activity, LC3-II flux) reported separately and never collapsed, plus baseline distal-axon alpha-tubulin acetylation, bidirectional cargo transport and axonal swelling counts in microfluidic culture.
next_actions.supports_if: A phenotype replicates across >=2 patient lines and >=2 independent differentiations. If the heterozygous-null line is normal while the missense line is abnormal, that is the dominant-negative signature and it licenses the lowering program. The same panel simultaneously tells you whether the lesion is recycling-type or degradative-type, and whether any transport deficit exists.
next_actions.kills_if: The heterozygous-null line phenocopies the patient — haploinsufficiency; terminate mutant lowering and reorient to raising wild-type strumpellin. If no readout separates patient from corrected neurons while positive controls respond, the blocker is the assay, not the hypothesis, and no therapeutic program should advance until a quantitative neuronal phenotype exists. Report that as uninformative, not negative.

next_actions.action: Run the allele-dosage arm on the established platform, using the ASO toolkit strictly as a mechanism probe rather than a drug candidate, and define the wild-type-loss tolerance curve once.
next_actions.question_answered: Is the therapeutic sign dominant-negative or haploinsufficiency, and how much wild-type strumpellin can a human neuron lose before a phenotype appears?
next_actions.activity_required: Design 3-5 gapmer RNase-H1 ASOs with positional chemistry for single-nucleotide discrimination at the mutant site (design precedent PMID:23963702; PMID:39027419), plus a total-WASHC5 ASO and non-targeting control. Gate on allele-resolved pharmacology by amplicon NGS/allele-specific ddPCR, requiring >=70% mutant knockdown with <=20% wild-type knockdown. Read the Action 2 phenotype panel across untreated patient, selective knockdown, total knockdown, corrected and heterozygous-null arms. Separately titrate total-WASHC5 knockdown across a dose range in control neurons to generate the dosage-sensitivity curve.
next_actions.supports_if: Mutant-selective knockdown moves the phenotype toward corrected; total knockdown gives no benefit or worsens; the heterozygous-null line is normal. Dominant-negative confirmed — the lowering program has its sign and a pharmacodynamic endpoint.
next_actions.kills_if: Selective knockdown gives no benefit while total knockdown worsens the phenotype, or the tolerance curve shows that even 20-30% wild-type loss produces a phenotype. The therapeutic window for lowering does not exist; terminate and redirect to wild-type raising.

next_actions.action: In parallel with Action 3 and at low cost, perform long-read single-molecule phasing of WASHC5 in all accessible SPG8 families to determine whether mutant alleles sit on a small number of shared haplotypes.
next_actions.question_answered: Can any allele-selective product serve more than one patient, or is SPG8 lowering permanently an n-of-1 proposition?
next_actions.activity_required: Long-read phasing of the mutation to candidate heterozygous target SNPs without requiring family data (workflow precedent PMID:33209959), analysed against the ancestry-aware haplotype-coverage template used in HD (PMID:31708117).
next_actions.supports_if: Mutant alleles cluster on a few common haplotypes, making a 2-3 SNP-directed product plausible and justifying a conventional development path if the sign is confirmed.
next_actions.kills_if: Every mutant allele is private and unphaseable to a shared haplotype. Accept n-of-1 mutation-directed ASO only, with a single committed family and a milasen-style regulatory path; do not plan a population product.

next_actions.action: Run the HDAC6 pharmacology arm only if Action 2 shows a baseline transport or tubulin-acetylation deficit, and require genotype-selective rescue.
next_actions.question_answered: Is a measured SPG8 transport deficit pharmacologically correctable in a disease-specific rather than generic way?
next_actions.activity_required: Dose-response with a selective CNS-penetrant HDAC6 inhibitor (EKZ-438-class, PMID:41061670; tubastatin A as tool comparator, PMID:29520015), dosing isogenic controls on the same plates, with acetylation increase measured as the pharmacodynamic control and distal neurite degeneration as the outcome.
next_actions.supports_if: Transport and distal degeneration normalise toward control with a significantly larger effect in SPG8 than in isogenic neurons at matched acetylation increase. Then — and only then — commission a patient-missense knock-in mouse before any clinical consideration.
next_actions.kills_if: No baseline deficit at Stage 1 (kills before any compound is purchased), or equal improvement in patient and control neurons at matched acetylation — a generic pharmacodynamic effect with no SPG8-specific benefit. Deprioritise HDAC6; retain any transport deficit as a biomarker for other agents.

next_actions.action: Add a surface-proteomics and conditioned-medium transfer screen to the existing isogenic neuron platform as a low-cost add-on, not as a protein-modality program.
next_actions.question_answered: Does any extracellular or cell-surface mediator sit between WASH-complex failure and distal axonal dieback — i.e. is there anything at all for a biologic to bind?
next_actions.activity_required: Cell-surface biotinylation plus mass spectrometry and secretome profiling of SPG8 versus isogenic-corrected cortical neurons; conditioned-medium transfer test for neurite-maintenance effects in both directions. One cell line pair, two assays, no animals, no biologic manufactured.
next_actions.supports_if: A reproducible, mechanism-linked surface receptor or secreted mediator is altered — plausibly a mis-sorted receptor retained or depleted at the surface as a consequence of WASH-dependent recycling failure — or conditioned medium transfers a maintenance deficit. This creates a genuine extracellular interface and justifies reopening the protein modality as a separate target.
next_actions.kills_if: No reproducible surface or secreted difference and no transferable medium effect — the likely outcome. Close the protein modality for SPG8 permanently; the perturbation is confirmed wholly intracellular.

do_not_fund_yet: Any CNS siRNA chemistry, di-siRNA architecture development or RNA-modality manufacturing for WASHC5. It duplicates the ASO arm's mechanistic question with a strictly worse CNS delivery position and no approved CNS siRNA precedent. Run the wild-type-loss tolerance curve once inside the ASO workstream instead.

The compound-exposure arm of the endolysosomal flux approach — rapamycin, everolimus, torin-1, trehalose screening. There is no demonstrated human SPG8 endolysosomal deficit to correct, no pharmacodynamic endpoint, no positive control to benchmark assay sensitivity, and a credible directional-harm mechanism in which a flux enhancer accelerates loss of cargo that WASH-dependent recycling should retrieve while the lysosomal biomarker improves.

Any protein or biologic program: trophic/receptor-agonist biologics, anti-Nogo-A/anti-RGMa/anti-LINGO-1 axon-inhibitor blockade, BBB-shuttle engineering, or strumpellin protein replacement. Replacement is mechanistically excluded for an obligate cytosolic complex subunit, and the remaining routes have no SPG8-specific rationale and no extracellular target.

GMP ASO manufacture, IND-enabling toxicology, or any n-of-1 regulatory filing. The sign of the intervention is not established; manufacturing before Action 3 reads out risks producing a drug that is at best neutral and at worst harmful.

A patient-missense knock-in mouse. This is the right eventual investment and the absence of an in vivo model is the shared ceiling on the whole dossier — but commission it only after a cellular phenotype exists and the therapeutic sign is fixed, so the model is built to report a readout you can interpret.

Any clinical trial planning, natural-history-independent endpoint development, or trial-readiness work for SPG8 therapeutics. With no biomarker, no animal model and an undetermined mechanism, trial design is premature. A natural history and genotype-phenotype registry, by contrast, is cheap, useful under every scenario, and would pair naturally with the Action 4 phasing effort.

Medicinal chemistry on novel HDAC6 inhibitors or any new chemical series. Selective CNS-penetrant tool compounds already exist and are sufficient for the Stage 2 question; new chemistry before a demonstrated genotype-selective effect would be spend on a pharmacodynamic effect that may be disease-irrelevant.
conclusion_note: The causal gene is secure, but the therapeutic sign is not: dominant-negative versus haploinsufficiency is unresolved and inverts every genetic intervention. Compounding this, no human SPG8 cell has been shown to have any measurable phenotype, and no in vivo model reproduces the disease — so there is currently no pharmacodynamic endpoint for any modality. The key contrary datum (no motor phenotype in heterozygous Washc5 knockout mice) is recalled rather than verified in full text and should be checked before it is relied upon. One shared isogenic iPSC trio — patient missense heterozygote, variant-corrected, heterozygous null — collapses most of this uncertainty at once and is the only thing that should be funded at scale now. Verdicts: INVESTIGATE for the allele-selective ASO and for the HDAC6 transport probe (opposite strengths: root mechanism with unproven delivery, versus proven delivery with unproven mechanism); LOW PRIORITY for the RNA duplicate and the endolysosomal flux compound arm; REJECT for the protein modality on categorical target-compartment grounds. No approach earns PURSUE, because in every case the dominant failure mode remains untested. This is decision support for researchers, not medical advice.
